source.title: VASAE: Naming SAE Dictionary Directions with Vocabulary-Aligned Anchoring
source.authors: Kai-Rui Zhang; Ziwen Yu; Z. Abdallah; M. Lewis

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests SAE reconstruction and feature recovery on GPT-2-small and Llama-3.1-8B, extending the sparse-feature question to LLM residual streams. It does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or test its superposition geometry directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reconstruction results for standard SAEs and VASAE, which bear on whether sparse dictionaries can recover real-model activations. The vocabulary-alignment rates and token-name case studies are produced by an explicit anchoring objective; they do not establish naturally occurring superposition or canonical SAE units. Hard-tied-decoder reconstruction results concern a different representation and are recorded under fits_no_version. LogitLens is a separate direct-readout diagnostic, not a measure of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It introduces VASAE, an SAE with a vocabulary-anchor loss that gives each feature a nearest-token name. It takes the superposition and SAE premise as given, citing Elhage et al. 2022 only as motivation. What it reports is its own method's performance: reconstruction matching a standard top-k SAE baseline, anchor-strength ablations, and induced token alignment. It never asks whether LLM activations contain sparse features, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAE features are canonical. The standard-SAE numbers appear only as a comparison baseline for VASAE. The alignment geometry is produced on purpose by the anchor objective. So no row bears on a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. VASAE matches standard-SAE reconstruction while giving strongly token-aligned features in GPT-2-small and shallow/middle Llama layers. The Llama alignment depends on the anchor coefficient and is unstable at the final layer. Token names are geometric handles, not causal interpretations.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains vocabulary-anchored and standard top-k SAEs on LLM residual streams; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method. It adds an anchor loss to SAE reconstruction and sparsity objectives.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction is reported across representative layers and anchor coefficients; the study states that changing the anchor coefficient from 0 to 5 × 10−3 changes VE and CE recovery only slightly on the representative layers.

fits_no_version.finding: A decoder hard-tied to token embeddings reconstructs residual streams far worse than learned dictionaries (GPT-2 VE −0.434, Llama VE −0.021; Table 1). No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream activations are not well spanned by a sparse code over exact token-embedding directions.

fits_no_version.finding: An anchor loss can pull most SAE decoder directions to within cosine 0.8 of token embeddings with no reconstruction cost: about 90% in GPT-2 L0–L10, and 92.8% at Llama L0 but limited at L31. This alignment is induced by the objective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries are non-unique: reconstruction-equivalent dictionaries with very different geometry exist. This bears on V5 only indirectly and is not tested as such.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the 2nd Workshop on Compositional Learning at ICML 2026
record.problems: Only two LLM families are tested. Aggregate Table 1 uncertainties are across layers, not random seeds. The reported Llama alignment analysis is limited to representative layers and remains unstable at the final layer. Reconstruction results show a trained SAE can approximate activations, but do not independently establish that its learned features are naturally occurring, stable, or canonical units.
record.rows_left_out: The layerwise diagnostics in Figure 5 are not separately rowed; they are plotted without tabulated layerwise values, and Table 1 and Table 2 already report aggregate and representative-layer reconstruction metrics. LogitLens accuracy is omitted because it is a direct-readout agreement measure, not a measure named by the tested claim version. Vocabulary-alignment rates and qualitative case studies are omitted because their geometry is deliberately induced by VASAE anchoring and does not test V4's natural-feature claim. Hard-tied decoder rows are listed under fits_no_version but are not included in rows.

untested.parts: Entire version: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry of superposed features.
Entire version: no capacity or importance analysis, no neuron-level polysemanticity.
Whether LLMs naturally spread features across neurons or contain recoverable sparse features. SAEs are used as a tool, and reconstruction is reported only to compare VASAE with a baseline.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features. The authors explicitly say token names are not feature explanations.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Downgraded from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper is a feature-naming method that presupposes SAEs. Every row is either the authors' method, its baseline, or a hyperparameter ablation. A lenient reader might count the standard-SAE rows (VE 0.965/0.931, CE rec 0.975/0.906 with k=32) as weak indirect V4 evidence. However, the paper neither frames nor analyses them that way, and reconstruction alone does not establish that features are natural. The reader's fits_no_version entry referenced nonexistent hard-tied rows; these row_ids were cleared. One citation-level link exists: a feature can share a token name with others, which is many-to-one naming.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether feature importance and limited capacity cause dedicated versus shared dimensions or neuron polysemanticity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

Tests reconstruction by trained sparse dictionaries on two LLM families, but not whether the models naturally organize features across neurons or whether learned features are independently present before dictionary training.
Does not test completeness, stability, or canonicality of SAE features. It cautions that a nearest-token name is not a feature explanation.
Uses one decoder column as a feature direction but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard SAE and VASAE reconstructions on GPT-2-small and Llama-3.1-8B, with aggregate results across layers and representative anchor-strength settings
reader_labels.reason: Both learned sparse dictionaries show substantial reconstruction and downstream-loss recovery; the paper reports VASAE metrics comparable to standard SAE. Rows t1-gpt-standard-ve, t1-gpt-standard-ce-rec, t1-gpt-vasae-ve, t1-gpt-vasae-ce-rec, t1-llama-standard-ve, t1-llama-standard-ce-rec, t1-llama-vasae-ve, and t1-llama-vasae-ce-rec, plus the representative sensitivity rows.
